summary: Hazrat Sultan International Airport (HSA) serves the historic city of Turkistan in southern Kazakhstan, a major pilgrimage and tourism destination. The airport was opened in 2020 to accommodate growing visitor traffic to the UNESCO World Heritage-listed Mausoleum of Khoja Ahmed Yasawi. It is one of Kazakhstan's newest international gateways and features modern terminal facilities suited to the region's increasing tourism demands.
faqs:
Q: Where is Hazrat Sultan International Airport located?
A: The airport is located near Turkistan in the Turkistan Region of southern Kazakhstan, approximately 10-15 km from the city center.

Q: What is the main attraction near this airport?
A: The Mausoleum of Khoja Ahmed Yasawi, a UNESCO World Heritage Site and one of the most important Islamic pilgrimage destinations in Central Asia, is located in Turkistan.

Q: How new is Hazrat Sultan International Airport?
A: The airport commenced operations in 2020, making it one of Kazakhstan's newest international airports.

Q: Does the airport offer international flights?
A: Yes, it is classified as an international airport with regular flights to destinations including cities in Turkey and other regional hubs.
transport_tips: Taxis and pre-booked transfers are the most common ways to reach Turkistan city center from the airport, with a typical journey taking around 15-20 minutes. Public bus services also connect the airport to the city. Rideshare apps and hotel-arranged pickups are widely available and recommended for first-time visitors.
local_tip: Visit the airport during off-peak hours if possible, as it can get busy around major religious holidays and tourism peaks when pilgrims flock to the Yasawi Mausoleum. Also, bring some local currency (tenge) in cash, as card acceptance outside the airport terminal in smaller establishments can be limited.
